name: Houston
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Houston: energy and trade due diligence, Texas Business Court support, asset tracing and fraud inquiries.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters connected to Houston: energy, petrochemical and energy transition counterparties, Gulf Coast trade and shipping, disputes before the Texas Business Court's Houston division and Harris County courts, and asset tracing. Scoped from Nashville, with Texas-licensed investigators engaged where fieldwork requires them.
intro: Houston is the largest city in Texas and the centre of a ten-county metropolitan area of about 7.9 million people, according to the Greater Houston Partnership's summary of 2025 Census Bureau population estimates. The city itself has about 2.4 million residents. Houston is known internationally as a centre of the oil and gas industry and, increasingly, of energy transition businesses, and it hosts 27 Fortune 500 headquarters, the Texas Medical Center and the Port of Houston, the busiest container port on the Gulf Coast. The Houston-Galveston customs district handled 353.7 billion dollars of trade in 2025, and more than 1,000 Houston companies report foreign ownership.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Houston because its energy, petrochemical, shipping and engineering businesses link Texas to Latin America, the Middle East, Africa and Asia. Typical triggers include due diligence on oil and gas operators, service companies, traders and project partners; background research on executives and investors in energy transition ventures; fact development for joint venture, royalty, construction and governance disputes, now heard in part by the Texas Business Court; inquiries into suspected procurement fraud, kickbacks or foreign bribery risk in international projects; and asset tracing against individuals and companies holding Texas real estate, vessels, equipment or interests in closely held entities.

matters.title: Energy counterparty and partner due diligence
matters.text: Ownership, management, litigation and regulatory history of Houston oil and gas operators, oilfield service companies, traders and energy transition developers, supporting acquisitions, farm-ins, joint ventures, offtake agreements and financing, with attention to links into higher-risk producing countries.

matters.title: International project bribery risk
matters.text: Research into agents, consultants, local partners and politically exposed persons connected to Houston-led projects abroad, identifying ownership links and red flags relevant to US foreign bribery and sanctions compliance, to support counsel advising on onboarding, investigations or disclosure decisions.

matters.title: Gulf Coast trade and shipping
matters.text: Background on traders, freight forwarders, vessel owners and charterers using the Port of Houston and Gulf Coast terminals, supporting lenders, insurers and counsel examining cargo loss, documentary fraud, export control concerns or payment default in commodity and petrochemical trades.

matters.title: Texas Business Court dispute support
matters.text: Fact development, chronologies and background research on parties and witnesses for governance, owner, derivative and high-value contract disputes before the Texas Business Court's Houston division or Harris County district courts, structured with Texas counsel for use in litigation and discovery planning.

matters.title: Asset tracing and judgment enforcement
matters.text: Research into Texas real property, entity interests, vessels, aircraft, equipment liens and litigation history to locate assets of individuals and companies in the Houston region, supporting creditors, receivers and counsel pursuing judgments or arbitral awards, including recognition of foreign awards.

local_context.title: Texas Business Court, Houston division
local_context.text: Created by legislation signed in June 2023, the Texas Business Court began operating in September 2024 as a statutory court separate from the district courts. The Eleventh Business Court Division sits in Houston and was among five divisions active from the start. It hears corporate governance, internal owner and derivative disputes and large commercial contract cases above monetary thresholds, which 2025 amendments lowered while adding intellectual property and trade secret matters. Appeals go to the Fifteenth Court of Appeals.

local_context.title: Harris County courts and records
local_context.text: Commercial litigation outside the Business Court is heard in the Harris County civil district courts, with the federal Southern District of Texas also sitting in Houston. County-level clerk records for real property, assumed business names and court filings are a principal source for asset and litigation research in the region, with access rules, fees and online availability varying by office and record type.

local_context.title: Texas investigator licensing
local_context.text: Texas licenses private investigators through the Private Security program of the Department of Public Safety under Chapter 1702 of the Occupations Code. According to DPS, an expert who conducts their own investigation to secure evidence for court must be licensed, while reviewing evidence already gathered by licensed investigators does not by itself require a licence. Fieldwork in Houston is therefore carried out by Texas-licensed investigators.

local_context.title: International and energy institutions
local_context.text: Houston's international business community includes 41 active foreign chambers of commerce, trade or commercial offices of eleven foreign governments, and nineteen foreign banks from ten countries, according to the Greater Houston Partnership. These networks, alongside energy industry associations and the Texas Medical Center, shape how counterparties are introduced and where reputational and commercial information about them can lawfully be found and verified.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Houston, TDSC first establishes whether the question is primarily a Texas one, such as a governance dispute or asset recovery, or an international one routed through Houston, such as an energy partner abroad or a cargo trade. Texas work draws on Secretary of State filings, Harris County and other county records, state and federal court dockets and open sources; international work extends to registries and sources in the producing or trading countries concerned. TDSC aligns with Texas counsel on forum, including the Texas Business Court, and on discovery. Where surveillance, interviews or other evidence-gathering in Texas is needed, TDSC engages investigators licensed by the Texas Department of Public Safety. TDSC has no office in Houston.

faqs.q: What is the Texas Business Court and does it sit in Houston?
faqs.a: It is a specialised statutory court that began operating in September 2024 to hear corporate governance, owner and large commercial disputes. Its Eleventh Division sits in Houston. Monetary thresholds and covered case types were adjusted by 2025 amendments, so Texas counsel should confirm whether a dispute qualifies before TDSC scopes supporting research.

faqs.q: Does investigative work in Houston require a Texas licence?
faqs.a: Securing evidence for use in court or similar investigative work for hire in Texas generally requires a licence from the Department of Public Safety's Private Security program under Chapter 1702 of the Occupations Code. TDSC engages Texas-licensed investigators for such work and scopes engagements so that its own consulting role stays within applicable limits.

faqs.q: Can TDSC research energy partners outside the United States for a Houston client?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Houston engagements concern operators, agents or partners in other producing countries. TDSC researches ownership, politically exposed person links, litigation and sanctions exposure through lawful public sources and, where needed, coordinates appropriately licensed professionals in the country concerned, screening every matter for US sanctions compliance.

faqs.q: How does TDSC help locate assets in the Houston area?
faqs.a: TDSC reviews county property records, Texas entity filings, lien and court records, vessel and aircraft registrations and open sources to identify assets and the entities that hold them. It does not access bank account data or restricted government systems; account-level information is pursued by counsel through lawful legal process.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Houston?
faqs.a: No. TDSC has no office, staff or address in Houston. Engagements are scoped and managed from Nashville, Tennessee. Where local fieldwork is required, TDSC coordinates investigators licensed in Texas and works with the client's Texas counsel under a written scope agreed in advance, before any work begins.
